subject: general
question: PX is a tangent drawn from point X, touches the circle at P, O is the centre of the circle. Radius of this circle is 10 cm and OX = 26 cm. What is the length of PX ?
solution:
**Given:**

PX is a tangent drawn from point X.

O is the centre of the circle.

Radius of this circle is 10 cm and OX = 26 cm.

**Concept Used:**

When a tangent is drawn from an external point to a circle, it forms a right angle with the radius drawn to the point of tangency.

Pythagoras theorem

Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular²

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6ee89817c09fc0578f923eafdd8cdd8eef34a8343800d5abe4a7c72a518ea676.png] 

Here PX is the tangent makes 90° angle with the radius.

In triangle OPX,

OP = 10 cm

OX = 26 cm

Apply Pythagoras theorem

Hypotenuse2 = Base2 + Perpendicular2

262 = 102 + Perpendicular2

Perpendicular² = 262 - 102 

Perpendicular2 = 676 - 100

Perpendicular2 = 576

Perpendicular = 24 cm

PX = 24 cm

**∴ Option 2 is the correct answer.**
